#!/bin/bash -l
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name=cice-qc
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -t 1:00:00
#flux: -q compute

# The Slurm output/error directives are combined into a single output file.
# The '%j' variable is replaced with Flux's '{job.id}'.
#flux: -o log-cice-qc.o{job.id}

# The following Slurm directive for account was not translated as it is not a standard Flux option.
# Account information is often handled by site-specific policies or plugins.
# #SBATCH -A e3sm

# The original script did not request CPUs per task, so it defaults to 1.
# This is preserved by not specifying a '-c' or '--cpus-per-task' option.

# The Flux equivalent of $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR is ${FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR}
cd $FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

source /lcrc/soft/climate/e3sm-unified/load_latest_e3sm_unified_chrysalis.sh

export HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE

export BASE=/lcrc/group/acme/ac.dcomeau/scratch/chrys/20221218.DMPAS-JRA1p5.TL319_EC30to60E2r2.chrysalis.column-package.intel/run
export TEST=/lcrc/group/acme/ac.dcomeau/scratch/chrys/20221218.DMPAS-JRA1p5.TL319_EC30to60E2r2.chrysalis.icepack.intel/run

# 'srun' is not needed for a single-task job; the command is run directly.
# The allocated resources are available to the script's environment.
python mpas-seaice.t-test.py $BASE $TEST

#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --time=1:00:00
#SBATCH -A e3sm
#SBATCH -p compute
#SBATCH --job-name=cice-qc
#SBATCH --output=log-cice-qc.o%j
#SBATCH --error=log-cice-qc.e%j

cd $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

source /lcrc/soft/climate/e3sm-unified/load_latest_e3sm_unified_chrysalis.sh

export HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE

export BASE=/lcrc/group/acme/ac.dcomeau/scratch/chrys/20221218.DMPAS-JRA1p5.TL319_EC30to60E2r2.chrysalis.column-package.intel/run
export TEST=/lcrc/group/acme/ac.dcomeau/scratch/chrys/20221218.DMPAS-JRA1p5.TL319_EC30to60E2r2.chrysalis.icepack.intel/run

srun -N 1 -n 1 python mpas-seaice.t-test.py $BASE $TEST
